query: The Fisherman Waves The old fisherman in the reed beds has never waved at a courier. Today, seeing the jar strapped to your broom, he waves, and beckons you down. "That jar," he says. "I flew it once. Fastest year of my life." Land and ask him about it He tells you, slowly, between casts: you don't fly the wind, you let it get behind you and keep going. Never stop. "Stopping's what kills it," he says, and goes back to his line. He talks about fish for an hour, then says the light's going, and rows off. You'll have to come back. Wave back and fly on You wave and fly on with your round, on time. He watches you go, and doesn't wave again.
